sections.title: Cost management & approval experience
paragraphs: Separated personal subscriptions, organizational budgets, AI Enterprise, model APIs, and infrastructure costs, and explored ways to show usage and spending by user, organization, model, and project. The aim was to record cost, benefit, security, and scope together to reduce duplicate adoption and unnecessary spending.

Analyzed AX Spend Gate's application, approval, and rejection screens and processes for a September 2026 improvement report. The main proposals were to clarify rejection reasons and revision/resubmission paths; show approval, rejection, and additional-information messages with next steps; notify organization leaders of approval, payment completion, and status; and prioritize confusing UI elements by their impact.

Planned the report around analysis findings → priority actions → follow-up proposals, and problem → impact → action. Discussed sharing it with owners and applying changes in stages; this does not mean every proposed UI change had already shipped.

Proposed a longer-term operating record linking each AI request to its tool owner, purpose, data/risk, approval, monthly cost, benefit, and next review date, with overspend alerts, approval authority, budget attribution, and ongoing monitoring.

sections.title: Approval criteria & selected changes

Challenged Giseok's proposal to standardize input fields across spending tiers using the relevant trade-offs, while keeping the discussion collaborative by sharing it with Serin and Gyeongyeong.
Supported improvements to approver notification wording.

Outcome: changes were implemented in the development environment, including an LLM Gateway option; inputs tailored to approval tiers; rejection-reason entry and confirmation fields; usage display in Slack App Home; and guidance-message UI changes.

projects.status: Analysis and selected development changes. The broader lifecycle record remains a proposal.

Usage growth outside the original target group raised a policy choice between encouraging productive use and constraining spend.

OpenAI API unit prices also fell outside the announcement’s scope, so the report avoided attributing every price reduction to the announcement.

Validated the finance submission, identified a material input error, and documented why the submitted amount differed from the baseline scenario.
Separated usage-based costs (API, Enterprise usage, Cursor) from seat-based costs. Kept annual personal subscriptions on an annual basis instead of presenting them as monthly spending.
Clarified that Bedrock credits would start later than the first forecast months and should not be treated as an immediate recurring discount.
